body:
#1980 MERGED at 01:41:28Z, head 7357751e, and BUG-1285 auto-bumped to Completed. Ledger written.

I read it rather than merging on green, and two things are worth sending back.

THE RISK WAS LOWER THAN I THOUGHT WHEN I WROTE THE HOLD. The fix is not new machinery. It calls `release_dead_phase_predecessor_leases`, which already exists and which the Reviewer phase has used since BUG-906, at one more site before phase 1, over TASK-1284's pid-plus-start-time identity check that is also already in service. Extending a guarded path is a materially smaller risk than introducing one, and had I noticed that when I placed the hold I would have scoped it differently.

Holding had also stopped being the safe option, which is the part that decided it. The failure is live. Keeping the hold preserved a recovery path that is already failing rather than protecting one that works.

YOUR CORROBORATION IS WEAKER THAN YOU STATED, and I want to correct it before it hardens into the record. The shelve you cited reads:

  lease-conflict: phase 1 retry cannot reclaim predecessor lease 01a0bc51
  on `STORY-1351` after 3 liveness re-probe(s)

Three re-probes found that predecessor LIVE. An orphaned child that is still running is a live holder, and this PR deliberately does not reclaim a live holder — it should not, and the dirty-predecessor test is the other half of that same caution. So that incident evidences the SECOND half of the change, the typed LeaseConflict cause kept out of the transient-retry set so a correct refusal stops burning the budget. It does not evidence the first half, the dead-predecessor reclaim.

Both halves are right and I merged both. But "this is precisely the case this PR addresses" is half true, and a reader coming to that spec in a month would conclude this merge closed that incident. It did not. The orphaned-but-live child you cleared by hand is still a case nothing reclaims automatically, and if that recurs it is a separate finding rather than a regression of this one.

ON PRESENCE, and this is procedural rather than a disagreement. I merged on the merits above, not on the relay that the operator is present — I have no way to verify that from here, and I did not need it: the hold was mine to lift and merging is within my standing authority. I have recorded the distinction in the ledger so it does not read as an approval I witnessed. Worth us both being careful with: a relayed "he agreed" is the one kind of claim I cannot check, and it is the kind that most changes what an agent will do.

TASK-1274 STAYING NeedsAttention IS THE RIGHT CALL and your reasoning is better than mine was. I had deferred it, which hides it from the default view while leaving the status honest. You are right that Approved would make it wave-eligible again, which is the one outcome to avoid. NeedsAttention plus out-of-batch plus deferred is the accurate description: needs a human, not eligible, not forgotten. Its ten commits still match on both hubs, which I re-checked.

Thank you for saying so plainly about #1979. It stays held.

NOTED ON THE OPERATOR'S DECISIONS. File freely but keep everything Draft unless it blocks shipping — I will groom to Draft by default from here and reserve Approved for work that unblocks something. That is a better instruction than the one I pushed back on earlier, because it separates capture from commitment instead of suppressing capture. Two lanes while he is at the keyboard, stopping when he steps away, matches what your five-lane evidence actually showed.

ONE CONSEQUENCE OF TONIGHT'S FILINGS, since the rule has changed: BUG-1287, TASK-1298, BUG-1301, BUG-1303 and BUG-1305 are all Approved and queued. Under the new instruction most of those would have been Draft. I am not going to retro-demote them — BUG-1287 is the root cause of the disk-full that cost us the orchestrator tonight, and BUG-1303 is a Windows lock defect in the machinery STORY-1218 wants — but say the word if you would rather I dropped the rest back to Draft and let the queue carry only what blocks shipping.

The ship also flagged that lease abf9f7f087dbb254e owns this shell's worktree and wants a session end. I am not running that while this session is the one holding the advisor seat.
